events.title: Hymen Lipman Patents the Pencil with Attached Eraser
events.description: On March 30, 1858, Hymen Lipman of Philadelphia received US patent No. 19,783 for a pencil with a rubber eraser attached to one end. The patent was later invalidated in court as merely a combination of existing items rather than a new invention.
events.significance: The design became a staple of everyday writing tools worldwide, even though the patent itself was later voided.

events.title: United States Purchases Alaska from Russia
events.description: Secretary of State William H. Seward signed a treaty with Russia to buy Alaska for $7.2 million, about two cents per acre. The deal was initially mocked by critics as 'Seward's Folly.'
events.significance: The acquisition added roughly 586,000 square miles to the United States, giving it vast natural resources, including gold and oil, and strategic Arctic positioning.

events.title: Fifteenth Amendment Is Ratified
events.description: The Fifteenth Amendment to the US Constitution was declared ratified on March 30, 1870, prohibiting the federal and state governments from denying a citizen the right to vote based on race, color, or previous condition of servitude.
events.significance: It was a landmark of Reconstruction that formally extended voting rights to Black men, though discriminatory practices like poll taxes and literacy tests later undermined its enforcement until the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

events.title: Birth of Vincent van Gogh
events.description: Dutch Post-Impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh was born in Groot-Zundert, Netherlands. He produced about 2,100 artworks in roughly a decade, including The Starry Night and Sunflowers.
events.significance: Though largely unrecognized in his lifetime, Van Gogh became one of the most influential figures in Western art, shaping Expressionism and modern art.

events.title: Assassination Attempt on President Ronald Reagan
events.description: Outside the Washington Hilton Hotel, John Hinckley Jr. shot President Ronald Reagan, press secretary James Brady, a Secret Service agent, and a police officer. Reagan was seriously wounded but recovered after surgery.
events.significance: The event led to increased scrutiny of presidential security and fueled gun control debate, including the eventual passage of the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act in 1993.
